notes: §1985:VII.3.8.4 GR1: "If the RECORD clause is not specified, the size of each data record is completely defined in the record description entry"; §1985:II.2.1.4.3 leaves the record type of such a file to the implementor ("it is implementor defined whether fixed length or variable length records are obtained"). No edition arm: at 85 as at 2023 a file whose entry writes no RECORD clause (FileModel.RecordContains and Varying both null) is sized from its record description entries alone - FileModel.RecordWidth is the widest description's physical width, the file is fixed length unless ImpliesVariableFormat finds a variable-length description, and the connector pads or cuts every record to that width (FileConnector.FitRecord). Probed at --std 85: an FD with 01 R5 PIC X(5) and 01 R10 PIC X(10) and no RECORD clause writes two 10-character records (20-byte file; the short record is sent as the whole record area), the fixed-length choice §1985:II.2.1.4.1 describes ("Fixed length records must contain the same number of character positions for all the records in the file"). The witness writes and reads back one 8-character record of an FD with no RECORD clause.

next.reason: 1985: 'If the RECORD clause is not specified, the size of each data record is completely defined in the record description entry.' No other 1985 rule fixes the length of such a file's records (GR2 binds only external files). 2023 instead assumes a clause: §2023:13.18.43.4 GR5 'an implicit format 1 or format 2 RECORD clause is assumed to be specified', chosen by the implementor, where an implied format 1 has 'integer-1 ... the record size of the largest record description entry' and so makes every record fixed-length at that size (§2023:13.18.43.4 GR6 'Integer-1 specifies the number of bytes contained in each record in the file'); §2023:13.18.43.4 GR2 'The implicit or explicit RECORD clause specifies the size of records in the record area'. Under an implied format 1 a shorter record no longer has its own described size: different result.
